baseline_models.focus_anchor: The construction لِوَجْهِ ٱللَّهِ positively directs نُطْعِمُ, while لَا نُرِيدُ مِنكُمْ negates both جَزَاءً and شُكُورًا as returns from the recipients.
baseline_models.mechanism: A concrete transfer of nourishment is governed by a Godward orientation and intention; material requital and recognitional praise are both removed from the recipient-facing side of the act.

activation_trace.role: Feeding another supplies the concrete benefaction whose return conditions are being defined.
Orientation and direction make God's face the positive vector of the act rather than a mere absence of self-interest.
The fixed divine name identifies the destination that replaces recipient-directed return.
Will and intention locate the denied transaction at the level of what the feeders seek.
Act-matching recompense supplies the material or reciprocal return explicitly refused from the recipients.
Recognition and praise supply the symbolic return refused alongside recompense.

changed_reading.before: The speakers feed generously and happen not to expect thanks.
changed_reading.after: The speakers positively orient the act toward God while deliberately clearing both payment and praise from the recipients' side of the relation.

baseline_models.focus_anchor: The phrase مِنكُمْ جَزَاءً makes the source of the refused return explicit, and the lexical inventory of ج ز ي includes debt collection and one party standing in to discharge another's due.
baseline_models.mechanism: Provision is transferred without converting the receiver into a debtor, substitute payer, or source of public standing for the giver.

activation_trace.role: Provision and livelihood broaden the food from an item exchanged into support of another's condition.
Demanding or collecting a debt supplies the creditor relation that the negation blocks.
Standing in and settling a due shows the recipient is not required to become the settlement for the gift.
Status and eminence supply the social capital that recipient praise could otherwise create for the giver.
Praise of a benefactor identifies the recognitional obligation released with the financial one.

changed_reading.before: No payment is expected for the meal.
changed_reading.after: The gift is structured so that the recipient cannot be collected from as a debtor or used to manufacture the giver's status.

baseline_models.focus_anchor: The negated نُرِيدُ is paired with a packet-supplied non-dominant ر د د mapping whose return image can be tested against جَزَاءً and the directional لِوَجْهِ construction.
baseline_models.mechanism: Provision moves outward to the receiver and intention points Godward, while the feeder declines any reverse flow back from the receiver.

activation_trace.role: Provision and livelihood supply the outward-moving benefit.
Direction gives the benefit and the intention distinguishable vectors.
The split-root image of returning or sending back supplies the exploratory reverse-flow mechanism under negation.
Matching recompense names the ordinary return leg that would close an exchange.

changed_reading.before: The feeders do not desire a reward.
changed_reading.after: The ayah diagrams a deliberately open circuit: provision reaches the recipient, orientation reaches toward God, and nothing is routed back from the recipient.

baseline_models.focus_anchor: The final وَلَا شُكُورًا is anchored not only in praise but also in ش ك ر images of thriving on little, showing its effect, and putting out new growth.
baseline_models.mechanism: The negation releases recipients from verbal gratitude and, more tentatively, from having to display that the food produced a morally or visibly successful outcome.

activation_trace.role: Actual feeding supplies the small material input whose demanded effect is in question.
Recognizing a favor supplies the ordinary interpersonal sense directly negated.
Thriving on little and visibly showing its effect supplies an exploratory image of performed impact.
Sprouting young growth turns the demanded response into a visible-yield image rather than words alone.

changed_reading.before: The recipients need not say thank you.
changed_reading.after: The recipients need not verbally recognize the benefactor and may not even be required to perform visible improvement as proof that the gift worked.

context_deltas.mechanism: The people addressed are marked by abasement, loss of a protecting relation, and captivity. Refusing debt and praise therefore prevents food from becoming leverage over people whose ability to reciprocate or refuse is already constrained.

activation_trace.role: Feeding another anchors the social transfer whose power effects are being tested.
Debt collection supplies the coercive relation explicitly disabled by the refusal of recompense.
The abasement of poverty identifies one recipient as socially exposed to a benefactor's leverage.
Severance from a caretaker identifies another recipient as lacking a protecting reciprocal relation.
Binding and confinement make the captive's constrained agency the sharpest case for a gift without claims.

structural_cues: 76:8 names the needy person, orphan, and captive immediately before 76:9 addresses the fed group as كُمْ and مِنكُمْ.
The denial covers both material recompense and symbolic gratitude, closing two common routes by which aid can become control.
context_deltas.reader_inference: Packet: three recipient roots supply abasement, guardian-loss, and confinement in the immediately preceding feeding scene; inference: the no-return formula functions as an anti-leverage safeguard; alternative: it may state inward sincerity without making a general social-power claim.

changed_reading.before: The ayah describes the feeders' private sincerity.
changed_reading.after: It also protects vulnerable recipients by refusing the debt, praise, and dependence through which a benefactor could control them.

context_deltas.mechanism: Godward intention is not only serene devotion: the adjacent first-person explanation joins it to anticipated harm, divine lordship, and the severity of a coming day. Human return is refused while accountability remains motivationally active.

activation_trace.role: Orientation and direction establish the Godward aim revised by the next ayah.
Will and intention identify the motivational register to which fear is added.
Fear as expectation of harm supplies an active motive rather than a decorative mood.
Lordship and sovereignty locate accountability with God rather than the recipients.
The day's calamitous severity gives the Godward orientation a future horizon with weight.

structural_cues: 76:9 and 76:10 use adjacent first-person plural declarations, إنما نطعمكم and إنا نخاف.
The move from لوجه الله to من ربنا keeps God as the relational pole while changing the affect from orientation to fear.
context_deltas.reader_inference: Packet: adjacency, shared first-person voice, Godward phrases, and fear of a severe day are explicit; inference: 76:10 supplies a coexisting motive for 76:9; alternative: the voices may be rhetorically grouped without every motive explaining every feeding act.

changed_reading.before: Feeding for God's face sounds like exclusively serene, reward-indifferent devotion.
changed_reading.after: Freedom from human payment coexists with fear of divine accountability; the act is non-transactional toward recipients but not motive-less.

context_deltas.mechanism: The two returns refused مِنكُمْ reappear with a different source and object: the actors' work receives recompense and recognition in the divine address. Reciprocity is displaced away from vulnerable recipients rather than erased from the surah.

activation_trace.role: Matching recompense names the first return explicitly refused from the fed people.
Recognition of a favor names the second recipient-sourced return explicitly refused.
The same act-matching recompense image returns as the declared divine outcome.
Work and earned action identify the actors' striving, not the fed persons, as the object evaluated.
Recognition and praise return in passive form as the actors' work is acknowledged.

structural_cues: 76:12 first narrates وَجَزَىٰهُم, and 76:22 then places both focus nouns together: جَزَاءً and مَّشْكُورًا.
The focus limits the denied source with مِنكُمْ; the later verses change the source of response rather than contradicting the denial.
context_deltas.reader_inference: Packet: exact root recurrence and a shift from recipient-sourced denial to divine recompense and acknowledged striving are explicit; inference: the return leg is reassigned to God; alternative: the later reward may vindicate the act narratively without being part of the feeders' own motivation.

changed_reading.before: The act stands outside recompense and gratitude altogether.
changed_reading.after: The act rejects collection from recipients while leaving recompense and recognition to God, who later names both.

context_deltas.mechanism: Human feeding sits inside a larger sequence in which the righteous first drink and are later given drink by their Lord. The feeders can therefore be read as relaying provision they themselves inhabit rather than dispensing an independently owned resource.

activation_trace.role: Provision and livelihood make the food part of a sustaining flow rather than a bare commodity.
Orientation allows the relayed provision to move to people while its attribution points to God.
Taking in liquid places the righteous themselves in the position of receivers before the feeding declaration.
Giving drink supplies the later divine-to-human movement of provision.
Nurturing, repairing, and completing identify the Lord as the sustaining source of that movement.

structural_cues: Drinking in 76:5-6 precedes human feeding in 76:8-9, while the Lord's giving drink in 76:21 follows it.
Food and drink repeatedly cross giver-receiver positions across the surah.
context_deltas.reader_inference: Packet: repeated ingestion and a final explicit Lord-to-human drink are supplied; inference: human feeding relays a provision stream the feeders also receive; alternative: the drinking scenes may frame reward before and after the act without implying a stewardship theory of the food.

changed_reading.before: The feeders give away resources that are simply theirs.
changed_reading.after: They appear as temporary relays in a provisioning order they also receive from, which helps explain why they claim no return from the next recipient.

context_deltas.mechanism: The refusal of immediate payment and praise becomes a temporal discipline: deliberate intention resists bringing return forward, while the surah contrasts love of the immediate with leaving a weighty day screened behind oneself.

activation_trace.role: Direction gives the feeding an horizon beyond the immediate recipients.
Gentleness and deliberate slowness supply a focus-root image for refusing hurried return.
Recompense supplies the return whose timing is re-read by the context.
Hastening and bringing forward define the immediate economy the feeding resists.
Leaving something supplies the active abandonment of the later horizon.
Covering a thing behind the back makes neglect of the future a spatial concealment.
Weight against lightness gives the deferred day the gravity lacking in quick social return.

structural_cues: 76:27 explicitly opposes loving العاجلة to leaving a heavy day behind.
The focus refuses the two fastest human confirmations of generosity: repayment and praise.
context_deltas.reader_inference: Packet: immediate love, abandonment, concealment-behind, and heaviness form a temporal-spatial contrast; inference: the focus refusal enacts resistance to immediate return; alternative: 76:27 may target worldly preference generally rather than the timing of charitable reciprocity specifically.

changed_reading.before: The speakers merely lack personal interest in reward.
changed_reading.after: Their refusal becomes resistance to an economy of immediate confirmation, maintaining orientation toward a concealed but weightier horizon.

context_deltas.mechanism: The feeders' negated desire is placed within the surah's final account of taking a path and of human willing depending on God's will. Their purified intention is thus responsive alignment, not autonomous moral self-authorship.

activation_trace.role: Will and intention anchor the focus claim about what the feeders do not seek.
Orientation makes intention a directed path rather than a self-contained mental state.
A traversable extended path supplies the enacted form of direction toward the Lord.
Will attached to a thing supplies the explicit dependency between human and divine willing.
The repeated fixed divine name identifies whose will conditions the human one.

structural_cues: 76:29 joins willing, taking, lordship, and path; 76:30 immediately qualifies human willing by God's willing.
The focus likewise joins negated human desire to a Godward direction.
context_deltas.reader_inference: Packet: distinct volition roots, a path to the Lord, and the explicit dependency of human will are supplied; inference: the final rule governs the feeders' intention retrospectively; alternative: 76:30 addresses human choosing generally and need not specify the psychology of the speakers in 76:9.

changed_reading.before: The speakers autonomously purify their own intention.
changed_reading.after: Their refusal of human return is an enacted Godward alignment whose very willing remains dependent on divine willing.

context_deltas.mechanism: The ش ك ر images of visible response and new growth are echoed by later radiance, vigorous garden growth, ripened harvest, and green vegetation. Yet those effects occur as God's gift to the feeders, not as proof demanded from the people they fed.

activation_trace.role: Thriving on little and showing its effect supplies the image of visible impact that the recipient is not asked to perform.
Sprouting young growth gives that performed impact an organic form.
Beauty and radiance supply a visible effect granted after the act.
Entwining and thrusting vegetation expands visible response into vigorous garden growth.
The nearness and arrival of harvest time supply matured yield rather than mere promise.
Tender green vegetation supplies the final visual echo of fresh growth.

structural_cues: After the refusal of شُكُورًا, 76:11-21 repeatedly renders the actors' outcome as visible radiance, garden yield, and greenness.
The fed recipients disappear from this display; the visible effects belong to the later divine response.
context_deltas.reader_inference: Packet: the focus root's visible-yield branches and a later cluster of radiance, growth, harvest, and green imagery are supplied; inference: demanded impact is shifted away from recipients and returned as divine gift; alternative: the garden imagery may be reward description with no intended activation of the non-praise ش ك ر branches.

changed_reading.before: No verbal thanks is required from the recipients.
changed_reading.after: Even visible flourishing is not demanded as evidence from them; flourishing appears later as a gift, not a condition attached to the food.

surprising_valid_outliers.containment: This uses the packet's non-dominant ج ز ز mapping for focus جَزَاءً, so it is form-distant and must not be rendered as an etymological replacement for recompense. It remains anchored in the focus word and gains a material echo from the later near-ripe harvest; downstream prose should mark it as a harvest analogy for refused extraction.
surprising_valid_outliers.focus_anchor: The focus جَزَاءً has a supplied split target whose branch images readiness for shearing or harvest, under the explicit لَا نُرِيدُ مِنكُمْ negation.

activation_trace.role: Readiness for shearing or harvest supplies the strange but packet-authorized image of extracting a matured return.
The arrival and nearness of harvest time gives that extraction image a visible context echo.
Dominant act-matching recompense contains the analogy by preserving the ordinary later return sense.

changed_reading.before: The feeders do not ask people to repay the meal.
changed_reading.after: Exploratorily, they refuse to harvest a human yield from those they feed; harvest arrives elsewhere as part of the divine outcome.

surprising_valid_outliers.containment: This couples the non-dominant ر د د return image under focus نُرِيدُ with ث و ب return/reward branches at the literal garments, so it is a cross-domain return-flow model rather than a lexical claim that the clothes simply mean recompense. It stays anchored in the focus's negated desire and recompense and should be rendered as a qualified material-poetic echo.
surprising_valid_outliers.focus_anchor: The focus refuses a return from recipients through لَا نُرِيدُ مِنكُمْ جَزَاءً, while its split ر و د inventory supplies a return image.

activation_trace.role: Returning or sending back supplies the reverse flow refused at the level of desire.
Act-matching recompense identifies what an ordinary return flow would carry.
Return to a place or state makes the later garments a material carrier for the return motif.
Reward returning to its worker connects the clothing root directly to a non-recipient recompense circuit.
Declared recompense confirms that return reappears after being refused from the recipients.

changed_reading.after: Exploratorily, the return refused from recipients comes back from another direction and even takes material form around the givers as clothing and reward.

strongest_changes: The recipient-specific refusal protects the needy person, orphan, and captive from debt and social leverage.
Recompense and gratitude are not erased: 76:22 reassigns both to God's acknowledgment of the actors' striving.
The immediate continuation adds fear of divine accountability to the God-facing motive.
The wider drink sequence makes human feeding readable as relayed provision rather than proprietorial largesse.
summary.what_was_special: The whole-surah packet made the exact denied roots ج ز ي and ش ك ر return together under a changed source, while split-root and growth branches exposed harvest, visible-yield, and return-flow models that a purely thematic reading would likely collapse.
remaining_uncertainties: The shared first-person voice strongly links 76:9-10, but the degree to which fear explains every speaker's act remains open.
The visible-growth, harvest, and clothing-return models depend on branch-level material analogy and should remain explicitly exploratory.
The later divine reward may be the feeders' operative horizon or only the narrator's vindication of an otherwise non-calculating act.
